subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the p-block elements?

options.text: They include non-metals and noble gases.
They are also called transition elements.
Their outermost configuration varies from ns²np¹ to ns²np⁶.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are also called transition elements.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **P-block elements** include non-metals, metalloids, and noble gases, but not transition elements.
 
• These elements belong to Groups **13 to 18** of the periodic table.
 
• The general electronic configuration of p-block elements is **ns²np¹ to ns²np⁶**.
 
• Transition elements, on the other hand, are d-block elements and are found in Groups 3 to 12, making the statement incorrect.
 
• The p-block contains a diverse range of elements with varying properties, including metals, metalloids, and non-metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **p-block Elements:**

 
 
• These elements are located on the right side of the periodic table, excluding helium.
 
• They show variable oxidation states and include some of the most reactive non-metals like fluorine and oxygen.
 
• The p-block includes halogens (Group 17) and noble gases (Group 18), which exhibit unique chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **d-block (Transition) Elements:**
 
 
• These elements are found in Groups 3 to 12 of the periodic table.
 
• Their general electronic configuration is (n-1)d¹–¹⁰ns¹–².
 
• They exhibit metallic properties and are known for forming colored compounds and acting as catalysts.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Grouping:**
 
 
• The periodic table is divided into s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block elements based on their outermost electron configurations.
 
• s-block contains Groups 1 and 2, p-block contains Groups 13 to 18, d-block contains Groups 3 to 12, and f-block consists of lanthanides and actinides.
 
 
 
• **Unique Properties of Noble Gases:**
 
 
• Noble gases (Group 18) are chemically inert due to their completely filled valence shells.
 
• They are used in various applications like lighting (neon lights) and cryogenics (liquid helium).
